name: Hubbell
headline: Makes the hardware that connects and protects the electric grid, earning 55% a year before tax on capital used.
what_it_does: Hubbell makes the hardware that utilities and electrical contractors use: arresters, insulators, connectors, switches, smart meters and protection controls for the grid, and wiring devices, boxes and fittings for buildings. Utility Solutions (Grid Infrastructure and Grid Automation) is about 63% of its $3.67 billion of 2025 sales and Electrical Solutions about 37%. Products are sold mainly through distributors or directly to utilities.
why_it_passed: It earns 40% to 55% before tax on the net tangible capital it uses (42% in 2021, 55% in 2025), and did so through the cycle.
Its position has held against its nearest rival across seventeen years of record, though the analysis calls the advantage moderate.
Its economics can be foreseen ten years out from slow-moving variables such as utility spending on the grid.
The analysis found no sign of dishonesty and judged management's ability modestly positive.
why_not_now: At $482.23 a share against a value range of $204 to $405, the price is above the top. A buyer would earn about 2.5% to 4.6% a year after tax on the cash the business produces, below a 30-year US Treasury bond (5.63%). The price assumes cash growing about 10% a year for ten years.
watch: Its recent profit level (2023 to 2025) is unproven, and its earlier profits were about flat from 2008 to 2017 while about $1.5 billion went into acquisitions.

It paid about $3.0 billion for NSI in 2026 (about 15.5 times expected earnings before interest, tax and depreciation), and goodwill and intangibles of $7.5 billion now exceed shareholders' equity of $3.9 billion.
It has bought back shares at prices above its value with no stated price discipline.
